notable_absence.finding: No edition qualifier appears anywhere on this page for the CBO itself, matching the reference page's own notable_absence (the EE-only gate on the server/ CBO page disappears entirely on Capella, with no substitute gate). This guide states plainly that 'The Cost-Based Optimizer is active by default,' consistent with no Capella edition axis existing at all.

cross_component_finding: This guide is a genuinely consistent restatement of the reference page (cost-based-optimizer.json), not a drifted one: the requiresPriorExecutionOf fact (UPDATE STATISTICS must run before the CBO's cost model is usable) is restated almost word-for-word ('Before you can use the Cost-Based Optimizer with a query, you must first gather the statistics that it needs' vs. the reference page's 'Before you can use the cost-based optimizer with a query, you must first gather the statistics that it needs' - only capitalization differs), and the same SELECT/UPDATE/DELETE/MERGE/INSERT-INTO-with-SELECT statement list is repeated identically. Where this guide differs constructively (not inconsistently) from the reference page is in adding two activation mechanisms not covered there: the Query tab's Query Options window (a UI toggle) and the CBQ Shell's `\SET -use_cbo` command - genuine guide-level 'how' content layered on top of the reference page's 'what/why'.
cross_product_finding: Notably, this guide OMITS both server-version-string citations that the n1ql/ reference page for the same feature carries verbatim ('In Couchbase Server 7.6 and later, the Query service automatically gathers statistics...' and 'available starting with Couchbase Server 8.0'). This guide instead states the statistics-gathering behavior with no version qualifier at all ('The Query Service automatically gathers statistics whenever an index is created or built, and you can update statistics at any time'). This is the opposite of the round's usual anomaly direction: here the guide layer correctly drops a Capella-inapplicable server-version citation that the reference layer had left in, rather than picking up a new one - a case worth flagging to whoever is tracking the server-version-citation docs-issue, since it shows the anomaly is not uniformly present across all pages describing the same feature.
